entries.name: Ai

alwaysVisibleFields.subtitleJa: ベテルの東に位置すると記されるカナンの町
alwaysVisibleFields.summaryJa: アイは、ベテルの東、ベト・アベンのそばにある町としてヨシュア記7:2に初めて現れます。本文はこの節で、ヨシュアが斥候を送った先として名を挙げます。
alwaysVisibleFields.identityNoteJa: 「アイ」は本文の地名です。遺跡エト・テルを同定候補とする説はありますが、発掘年代との不整合を指摘する見解もあり、所在地は確定していません。
alwaysVisibleFields.historicalRoleJa: ヨシュア記7章ではベテル東方の町として位置づけられます。
alwaysVisibleFields.modernLocationJa: 古代カナンの中央高地にあった町。エト・テルなどが候補地とされますが、本文のアイとの同定には異論があります。
alwaysVisibleFields.locationNoteJa: 地図に点が表示される場合も、所在地を示す確定位置ではなく、従来資料に基づく参考位置です。

facts.textJa: ヨシュア記8:28は、占領後に町を焼き、廃墟の丘にしたと記します。
ギブオンの住民は、エリコとアイに対して行われたことを聞いたと記されています。
エルサレム王は、ヨシュアがアイを取り、王を処刑したと聞いたと記されます。
征服された王の一覧にもアイの王が挙げられます。

alwaysVisibleFields.summaryJa: ギレアドは、ヨシュア記12:2でシホンが支配した地域として現れ、本文はその範囲をヤボク川までと述べます。ここでは都市ではなく、時期や用法によって広さに幅のある歴史的地域名として扱います。
alwaysVisibleFields.identityNoteJa: ヨルダン川東側一帯を指す広い用法と、より狭いギレアド山地の範囲は区別し、現代国家・行政境界と同一視しません。
alwaysVisibleFields.historicalRoleJa: ヨシュア記12:2でシホンが治めた地域の半分として挙げられます。
alwaysVisibleFields.modernLocationJa: 歴史的地域はおおむねヨルダン川東側の山地に置かれますが、本文の用法は半ギレアドから東岸一帯まで幅があります。現代のヨルダン北西部と重なる範囲もありますが、古代の境界・行政区分を現在の州境と同一視できません。旧候補点は地域内の参考点としてのみ表示します。
alwaysVisibleFields.locationNoteJa: 地図に点が表示される場合も、所在地を示す確定位置ではなく、従来資料に基づく参考位置です。

facts.textJa: ヨシュア記12:5は、バシャンのオグ王の支配範囲がシホンのギレアドとの境界に及んだと記します。
ヨシュア記13:11は、ギレアドをゲシュル人・マアカ人の境界やヘルモン山、バシャンと並べて挙げます。
ヨシュア記13:25では、ガドの境界にギレアドの諸町とアンモン領の半分が含まれると記されます。
ヨシュア記13:31では、ギレアドの半分がマナセの子マキルの一族に割り当てられたと記されます。
ヨシュア記17:5は、マナセの割当地に加えてヨルダン川の向こう側のギレアドとバシャンを挙げます。
17:6はギレアドの土地がマナセの残りの子らに属したと続けます。
ヨシュア記20:8は、ガド族領内のギレアドにあるラモトを逃れの町として挙げます。
ヨシュア記21:38はギレアドのラモトを放牧地付きのレビ人の町として挙げます。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Wikipedia introduction identifies Adullam as an ancient Canaanite city (Josh 12:7–24; 15:35). Its identification section says Upper Adullam remains inconclusive and distinguishes a lower site accepted by historical geographers; this is compatible with retaining archaeological location uncertainty.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Article identity supported; keep location uncertainty and do not equate the cave tradition with the city.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The article says Ai was a Canaanite city in the Hebrew Bible and that Et-Tell is the common identification, while excavation chronology leads scholars to interpret Joshua’s conquest account as etiological myth.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Identity supported, but archaeological identification is disputed; current profile’s uncertainty is appropriate.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The article identifies Anathoth as a Levitical town for Aaron’s descendants in Benjamin, notes a person-name homonym, and gives Anata as a traditional identification while also mentioning Abu Ghosh association.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong article identity match; multiple modern identification proposals mean no certainty upgrade.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The article distinguishes contemporary southern Arava usage from an older broad use spanning the Jordan Rift Valley between the Sea of Galilee and Gulf of Aqaba, including the Dead Sea.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Region article is relevant; profile correctly treats Biblical usage as broad/contextual and not identical to modern narrow area.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The article explicitly distinguishes two Transjordanian Aroer cities: one by the Arnon (identified with Ara’ir) and a second Ammonite/Gad-border city whose precise location is lost. Its Joshua-specific paragraph assigns that second city to the Gad–Ammon border.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: The JOS13:25 profile is the second Aroer; identity note correctly separates the Arnon site. Location remains unknown.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The article identifies Azekah as an ancient Judahite town and Tel Azekah/Tell Zakariya as a widely accepted identification, but its history records earlier reservations and other arguments. Joshua section directly associates it with Joshua10 and Judah15:20.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Article identity supported with qualification. Existing fail finding about future 15:35 in always-visible identityNote remains valid until author repair; do not treat this article check as fixing future-gate issue.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article names the town in Joshua19:8 among Simeon’s towns; says MT reads “Baalath-beer Ramath-negeb” while one LXX version reads “Baalath as you come to Ramath-negeb”; archaeological identification is unsettled and relationship to Ramath-negeb/Baal ambiguous.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong identity match; draft appropriately preserves textual and location uncertainty.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article describes Bamoth-Baal as an elevated location in Moab and says it is the first of three places where Balaam gives an oracle in Numbers22:41; categories include Joshua locations and Reuben.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Relevant article; note the article’s direct narrative emphasis is Numbers22:41, while this profile’s Joshua13:17 town-list use is supported by fixed WEB, not the article alone.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Resolved article is titled Bnei Brak. It says the modern city takes its name from ancient Biblical Beneberak in Joshua19:45 and was founded about 4 km from the Biblical site.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Relevant relation page, not identity of the modern city with the ancient site. Current profile distinguishes them and is supported.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article introduction says Beth Shemesh is the name of three places in the Land of Israel and one in Egypt; lists Judah, Naphtali, Issachar; the Issachar town is cited with Joshua19:22 and a possible Ain esh-Shemsiyeh identification.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: The generic article explicitly disambiguates the JOS19:22 Issachar town; profile’s identity is correct. For the Judah profile JOS15:10, its separate Tel Beit Shemesh link must be checked against that target rather than this generic article.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The lead identifies ancient Ashdod as a Levantine city whose remains are at Tel Ashdod, several kilometres south of modern Ashdod, supporting ancient/modern distinction. A later article section states Ashdod is listed among Judah-assigned cities in Joshua11:21–22; that claim conflicts with the actual fixed WEB JOS11:22, which names Ashdod only as a remaining Anakim settlement, so do not rely on the article for that biblical assignment.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Target city article is relevant; explicitly preserve the fixed-WEB correction to Wikipedia’s apparent Joshua 11 misreading.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Lead calls Beeroth a Biblical city, lists Joshua9:17 and 18:25, says it was an ancient Hivite settlement; later lines tie it to the Gibeonite confederacy in Joshua9 and later Benjamin inheritance in Joshua18. It says no known ruins and location is disputed.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Identity is supported, but exposing Joshua18:25 before knownBy JOS9:17 is a real future-gate issue until removed/gated in current profile.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The Hebrew Bible section directly calls Beit Shemesh the city in Judah on the border with Dan in Joshua15:10, and says that same city was set aside as one of the Kohanic cities in Joshua21:16.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Article matches the Judah town in JOS15:10; later JOS19:22 Issachar homonym should not be inserted into its always-visible identity note before that gate.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article identifies Hormah/Zephath as an unidentified city, cites Numbers14:45 and 21:2–3, and gives several competing locations; one discussion allows it could be a district rather than one town.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Relevant identity with genuine uncertainty; profile should gate later Joshua appearances (15:30,19:4) beyond initial JOS12:14.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: The page has a distinct “Town of Kanah” section identifying an Asher territory town in Joshua19:28 and a possible Ain-Kana site; this is separate from the article’s border river topic.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Current JOS16:8 is the stream/border candidate; direct article target is about a distinct later town and cannot alone establish that the river is that town. Keep relationship/location cautious and gate the JOS19:28 homonym.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Resolved page title/lead is the modern country Lebanon; the page includes modern country coordinates and physical geography, and the fragment URL is an etymology anchor on that modern-state article.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: This is only related-name support for ancient Lebanon; it is not the ancient range/region identity page and its country point must not be used as ancient geography. Current initial JOS1:4 profile must also not expose the later geographic extent from JOS13:5–6.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article’s narrative says first mention is Genesis32:2, where Jacob names the place; later section gives several David-era uses and the title “Mahanaim” is related to two camps.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Article identity matches the place but is not independent proof of JOS13 first use. Its later narrative must not be used as ungated historicalRole at JOS13:26; Levitical allocation is JOS21:38.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Japanese page states Gibbethon is an Old Testament toponym and a town in Dan’s inheritance; gives Tel el-Melate as a proposed identification. It also says it is a Kohathite Levitical city, then narrates Nadab/Baasha and later Omri events.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong target-page identity. Later Levitical-city role is after first profile use JOS19:44 and must be gated at 21:23; exact modern site remains an asserted proposal, not a verified coordinate.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article identifies Naphtali as one of the twelve tribes and describes its territory as eastern Galilee, west of Sea of Galilee, bounded by Asher/Dan/Zebulun/Jordan; references Joshua19:32–39.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Related collective/territory page; profile must clearly distinguish tribe from territory and support the geographic extent with all appropriate boundary verses rather than treating 19:32 tribe formula as a place occurrence.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Mephaath row: Joshua 13:18 and 21:37, Reuben, Levitical city; Umm ar-Rasas is suggested.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Shared table entry is secondary/wiki evidence only; candidate site or tentative equation is not independent coordinate confirmation.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Exact table matches include Beth-Hoglah JOS15:6/18:19,21; Bethul JOS19:4 and an unresolved equation with Chesil; Judah Debir JOS10:38–39 etc with a separate uncertain northern-border Debir entry; En-Tappuah JOS17:7 and its proposed equation with Tappuah; Gederothaim JOS15:36; Hazar-Gaddah JOS15:27; Hazor has separate Judah entries (JOS15:23 and 15:25) and Naphtali city (JOS11:1 etc); Hezron JOS15:3/25 possibly connected to Hazor2/Kerioth-Hezron; Idalah JOS19:15 Zebulun; Ir-Shemesh JOS19:41 Dan; Ithnan JOS15:23 Judah; Jabneel has Judah JOS15:11 and Naphtali JOS19:33 distinct; Janim/Janum JOS15:53; Jezreel has Judah JOS15:56 and Issachar JOS17:16/19:18 distinct; Kartah JOS21:34 Zebulun may be equated with Chisloth-Tabor. `Gaash` was only found in a reference to the hill north of Timnathserah, not as a city-list row; `Hepher` search returned Gittah-Hepher and a reference citation rather than an unambiguous row; `Kain` did not yield a matching entry; `Eglon` occurred in neighboring notes, not an unambiguous row.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Rows support textual identity/tribal distinctions, but table itself marks uncertain locations/equations and must not serve as coordinate verification. Gaash is a hill, not a city row; table lookup is related context only. Eglon, Hepher, and Kain remain unresolved by this targeted search.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Lead describes Akrabbim/Acrabbim as probably a general name for a ridge/pass between the south Dead Sea and Zin/Negev; directly calls it Maaleh-acrabbim in Joshua15:3 and ascent of Akrabbim in Numbers34:4.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong category match as a ridge/pass, not a city; coordinate on article may be a broad point only.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article calls Azmon a Biblical site marking a western segment of Judah’s southern frontier; cites Numbers34:4–5 and Joshua15:4, and proposes oasis Gusayma as a possible relation.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Identity is directly supported, but site/oasis relation remains proposal; profile should preserve uncertain location.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article lists two separate Beth Dagon cities: Judah (Joshua15:41), with uncertain site, and Asher (Joshua19:27) near Zebulun/Acre, with Beit Jann proposed.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: JOS19:27 profile correctly targets the Asher homonym; article is strongly relevant but contains both entities.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article says Bethoron names two neighboring towns on the Gibeon–Aijalon road; Upper Bethoron appears in Joshua16:5, Lower in 16:3; identifies them respectively with Beit Ur al-Fauqa and al-Tahta.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: The JOS16:5 profile is the Upper town. Do not use the generic map pin as the Lower town; page distinguishes the modern sites.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article identifies Bozkath as a Judah town in the Shephelah; cites Joshua15:39; notes one proposed site was rejected and precise location cannot be determined confidently.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong identity match; retaining location as unknown is correct.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Japanese article identifies the northern town Dan with Tel el-Qadi/Tel Dan and says it was formerly Laish (Leshem), captured and renamed by Danites; it distinguishes the group Dan tribe.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Relevant article for JOS19:47 town after rename. It also includes much later religious/history material, which must stay out of initial profile unless gated.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article lead describes Edom as an ancient kingdom across areas now in southern Israel, Jordan, and Palestine, and separately notes Edom/Edomites in ancient texts.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Relevant support for an ancient region/kingdom; its broad modern footprint and political identity must not be rendered as a precise city point or current national border.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Requested Edrei URL redirects to Daraa. Daraa article states that the Hebrew Bible calls the ancient city Edrei and describes it as capital of Bashan, site of the battle where Israelites defeated Og.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Matches the profile’s Bashan Edrei at JOS12:4; this does not identify the distinct Naphtali Edrei in JOS19:37. Redirected title should be clearly treated as same ancient city/Daraa relation, not page title identity alone.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article calls Eshtemoa an ancient city in the Judaean Mountains and says Joshua treats it as a Levitical city of Judah, citing Joshua15:50 and 21:14.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong town-identity support; this article’s account includes later Levitical allotment, so ensure the profile’s knownBy and always-visible fields do not expose the later assignment before its gate.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Geography section gives broad Galilee limits but says extent can be defined in stricter geological or more fluid historical/political terms; also shows eastern/western and northern/southern boundary variants.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Related regional evidence; modern Galilee borders cannot be equated with the ancient geography in Joshua. Profile’s geographic uncertainty wording is warranted.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article explicitly says Geshur was a territory in the ancient Levant, in the region of modern Golan Heights; identifies it along the eastern Sea of Galilee toward Yarmuk, and cites Joshua13:13, while distinguishing modern Geshur settlement and Iranian village.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Direct regional identity support; keep category as territory and avoid point-level precision or conflating later kingdom narrative with JOS13 context.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article lead identifies ancient village Huqoq and Joshua19; its Bible section cites Joshua19:34 but says the Yaquq identification is plausible while noting it may lie too far from Aznoth-Tabor to fit the boundary.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong name/verse match; site identification is qualified and should not be elevated to certainty.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Article identifies Jattir/Yattir as a Judean town and equates it with Khirbet Attir, an archaeological site; Joshua15:48 says it lies in Judah’s hill country.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong page match; ancient town vs archaeological/modern site should remain explicitly framed as identification.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Section says the ancient settlement of Jerusalem was, according to the Bible, named Jebus; this is a direct relation between Jebus and Jerusalem, not an unrelated city article.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Relevant relation evidence; because it is a Jerusalem section, do not conflate the profile’s ancient Jebus name with a separate coordinate/site.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: “In Judah” section says a Joktheel is mentioned in Joshua and 2 Kings and is located in Judah’s low country between Mizpah and Lachish (Joshua15:38); article separately has an Edom/Sela Joktheel.
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: Strong match for JOS15:38 Judah town; the profile should explicitly retain distinction from the Edom/Sela homonym.

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 日本語記事はアブドンを人物または町として説明し、町の項目でヨシュア記21:27–30、アシェル族のレビ人の町、二つの遺跡候補を記す。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象の町を同名人物から区別する点で一致。位置候補は確定扱いしない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はAchshaphをカナン北部の王都とし、ヨシュア記11:1、12:20、19:25を挙げる。Tel Keisanを候補位置として掲げる。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象地名の同定を支持。Tel Keisanは記事上の候補にとどめる。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はアダミ・ネケブをヨシュア記19:33のナフタリ境界上の地名として明記し、同節の隣接地名から位置を説明する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 直接一致するが、記事自体に出典不足警告があるため地理的確度は限定。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はAnavをヨシュア記11:21のユダ山地の町、15:50のユダ領の町として説明する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: プロフィール対象の町と一致。遺跡比定の確度は別途留保。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はBeth-Zurを南ユダの聖書遺跡とし、Khirbet et-Tubeiqaと同定されると記す。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象の町と一致。座標・考古学上の独立確定を意味しない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Lo-debar記事の本文は、ガド領のDebir（ヨシュア記13:26）と同一視する説を扱う。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: プロフィールがユダのDebirなら同一対象ではなく、関連記事にとどまる。同名地を統合しない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 開いたEgypt記事のHistory節は古代エジプト史の総説だが、本文検索でJoshuaへの言及は見つからなかった。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 関連する一般史記事であり、ヨシュア記の対象領域の直接同定根拠にはならない。関連記事扱いとする。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 日本語記事の冒頭はゲゼルを旧約聖書に登場する地名と説明し、記事題は「ゲゼル（聖書）」。検索した箇所では「ヨシュア記」という語は確認できなかった。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 聖書地名記事として関連するが、担当用例との書内同定を明示する直接根拠は限定。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 開いた記事はGileadという地理名の総説で、記事冒頭に地域座標を示す。今回検索した本文にJoshuaへの言及は見つからなかった。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 広域名の記事として関係はあるが、ヨシュア記の特定用例を同定する根拠にはしない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はヘルモン山をヨシュア記12:1・13:11におけるアモリ王国北境の山として記述する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象地形と一致。部族境界等のプロフィール説明は独立の聖書照合に基づける。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事は南部の「land/Mount Seir」とヨシュア記15:10にあるユダ北境の別のMount Seirを明確に分ける。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: プロフィール対象が南部山地なら区別に有用。北部の同名地点へ座標を流用しない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 日本語記事はキルヤト・エアリムを聖書の町とし、キルヤト・バアル等の別名および現在のデイル・エル＝アザル（テル・キルヤト・エアリム）との同一視を説明する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象の町を支持。ただし現代遺跡同定は記事が示す説として扱う。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: Names節は「sea of Kineret」をヨシュア記13:27の水域名として、Kinneretをヨシュア記19:35の町名として別々に記す。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: プロフィールが湖を指す場合は対象が一致し、同名町との混同も回避できる。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はSecacahをユダ荒野の町として説明し、ヨシュア記15:61を挙げる。Khirbet Qumranとの同定は一部研究者の説と記す。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象町の同定に一致。位置の説は確定として扱わない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 日本語のサイダ記事は現代レバノンの都市の記事で、カテゴリには聖書地名・古都・フェニキア都市を含む。本文表示箇所からヨシュア記の用例との同一性は確認できなかった。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 現代都市／古代シドンの歴史的連続性を扱う関連記事。書内の境界用例の直接根拠としない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はティルツァをヨシュア記で王を持つ町として最初に言及される古代都市と記す。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象の古代都市名と一致。候補遺跡や年代比定は別途不確実性を保つ。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事は上・下ベト・ホロンを境界沿いの二町として説明し、両町がエフライム族に属したとする。上り坂の地形も別節で説明する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 記事が二つの町と峠を併記するため、プロフィールの地点種別が「上の町」か「坂道」かを混同しない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はアコルの谷について複数の候補を挙げ、ヨシュア記の物語上の場所とユダ／ベニヤミン境界の位置づけに緊張があると明示する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 名称は一致するが、位置は記事内でも争点。候補を確定地点として扱わない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事の記述は谷をヨシュア記15:8のユダ・ベニヤミン境界とし、後代にTophet等の歴史を持つと説明する。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 関連節は対象地形に関係するが、記事全体の主題Gehennaと地理上の谷を混同しない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事本文はMizpahをGileadの地域、ヘルモン山麓のHivitesの居住地として記述し、ヨシュア記11:3・8を挙げる。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: プロフィールがヨシュア記11章のミツパを指すなら記事と合致。より南東のギルアドのミツパ等との同一視はしない。

wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.bodyExcerpt: 記事はヨシュア記15:8・18:16の谷をエルサレムから南西へ下る地形として記す。
wikiBodyChecksCurrentPass.assessment: 対象谷名と用例が一致。現代の同名地域・居住区とは区別する。
